answer.label: Nearly — Alcott’s wording is slightly different
answer.sourceLine: Alcott wrote the underlying sentence as Rebecca’s dialogue in An Old-fashioned Girl. The displayed version slightly modernizes and expands that wording; it is not a false attribution to a different author.

source.heading: The source
source.excerpt: “No, we have had enough of that; women have been called queens a long time, but the kingdom given them is n’t worth ruling,” answered Rebecca.
trail: The novel prints Rebecca’s reply without for before a long time. An Old-fashioned Girl primary text ↗
Wikiquote gives the modernized sentence and identifies the novel as 1870, chapter 13. Wikiquote source entry ↗
source.excerptNote: The source prints the contraction as is n’t/is n't. The displayed standalone form adds for before a long time; its attribution is right but it is not an exact transcription of this edition.
source.rightsNote: The documented text comes from a work published before 1931 and is public domain in the United States.

misattribution.truthLine: Credit Alcott and Rebecca’s dialogue; use the documented wording ↗ when claiming a verbatim quotation.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Rebecca is discussing a sculpture of a woman and rejects the suggestion that it needs a sceptre. Her response challenges ceremonial praise of women when the actual sphere available to them remains restricted.
